name: New York City
intro: You don't have to leave the metro area to see a big waterfall from New York City. The Great Falls of the Passaic in Paterson, New Jersey, sits about 17 miles from Manhattan inside Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park, and you can see it from overlooks a short walk from the street. It's the easiest waterfall trip from the city, and it can be done by train and bus.

For a full day, most New Yorkers head northwest. The Pennsylvania side of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, about an hour and a half to two hours by car in light traffic, has Dingmans, Silverthread and Raymondskill Falls within a few miles of each other, and the privately owned Bushkill Falls charges admission for a network of trails past eight falls. North of the city, Awosting Falls and Stony Kill Falls in the Shawangunk Ridge area pair well with a hike at Minnewaska State Park Preserve.
Flow is strongest in spring and after heavy rain. Many of these streams drop to a trickle by late summer, so a wet week in April or May beats a dry weekend in August.

name: Los Angeles
intro: Los Angeles waterfalls are seasonal. Most of the falls within reach of the city are fed by winter storms and snowmelt in the San Gabriel and San Bernardino Mountains, so they run best from about January through spring and can shrink to a damp rock face by late summer and fall. Plan a visit for the days after a good rain.

The closest is Sturtevant Falls in Big Santa Anita Canyon above Sierra Madre, about 17 miles from downtown in the Angeles National Forest. San Antonio Falls sits just off the road to Mount Baldy, and Bonita Falls is in Lytle Creek Canyon near the 15 freeway. Farther out, Big Falls in the San Bernardino Mountains, Rose Valley Falls above Ojai and Tahquitz Falls in Palm Springs each make a full day.
Mountain roads in these canyons can close after storms and fires, and forest parking areas may require a recreation pass. Check the managing agency's alerts before you drive.

name: Philadelphia
intro: Philadelphia has no big waterfall inside the city, but you don't have to drive far for one. The closest on our list is Gilpins Falls in North East, Maryland, about 47 miles southwest in a straight line, where Northeast Creek drops beside a restored covered bridge. It makes an easy half-day trip down I-95.

For a full day, head north. The Poconos hold most of the falls within reach of the city: Hawk Falls in Hickory Run State Park is a short hike off the Pennsylvania Turnpike's Northeast Extension, and the privately owned Bushkill Falls sells tickets for trails past eight falls. Farther up, Raymondskill Falls sits in Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, along with Dingmans Falls, whose trail has been closed for reconstruction since May 2025. The Great Falls of the Passaic in Paterson, New Jersey, is about as far as the Poconos and can be seen from overlooks near the street.
Spring and the days after a soaking rain are the time to go. Several of these streams run low by late summer, and Pocono roads and trails can be icy well into March.

name: Seattle
intro: Seattle is one of the best big cities in the country for waterfalls. Snoqualmie Falls, about 23 miles east of downtown in a straight line, drops 268 feet beside a free viewing area and is a short walk from parking. Keep going east on I-90 and Twin Falls, Teneriffe Falls and Franklin Falls are all short-to-moderate hikes off the interstate.

Farther out, US 2 passes Deception Falls east of Gold Bar, Mount Rainier National Park has Narada and Christine Falls right off the road to Paradise, and Olympic National Park's Marymere and Sol Duc Falls make a long day or an overnight from the city. Up north, Nooksack Falls is on the Mount Baker Highway.

Flow is highest from late fall through spring, when rain and snowmelt feed the Cascades. National forest trailheads usually need a Northwest Forest Pass or day pass, state parks need a Discover Pass, and the national parks charge entrance fees, so check which one covers your stop. Winter snow closes some trailhead roads, including Franklin Falls's.

name: Portland
intro: Portland sits closer to a dense stretch of public waterfalls than almost any other big U.S. city. Multnomah Falls, the most reviewed waterfall in the country on this site, is about 27 miles east in the Columbia River Gorge, and the Historic Columbia River Highway strings Latourell, Bridal Veil and Horsetail Falls within a few miles of each other. You can see several of them in a morning without leaving paved paths.

Farther out, still inside a two-hour radius, Sahalie and Koosah Falls on the McKenzie River and Narada Falls on the road to Paradise in Mount Rainier National Park make full-day drives. Closer south and west, Abiqua Falls, Drift Creek Falls and Moulton Falls fill in shorter trips when Gorge parking is packed.

Gorge flow is strongest in winter and spring. Summer brings timed-entry rules at Multnomah's I-84 lot and heavy traffic on the Historic Highway, so weekday starts and early arrivals matter more than they do in March.

name: Atlanta
intro: Atlanta does not have a famous waterfall inside the city limits, but north Georgia's national forest and state parks put several strong day trips within about an hour and a half. Amicalola Falls, Georgia's tallest cascade at 729 feet, is about 57 miles north in Amicalola Falls State Park, with a short accessible overlook trail if you skip the 604 stairs. Anna Ruby Falls near Helen and Helton Creek Falls near Vogel State Park sit a little farther out in Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest.

West and northwest, Noccalula Falls in Gadsden and De Soto Falls near Fort Payne, Alabama, stretch the same radius and pair well with a Talladega or Little River Canyon loop. Most of these stops are short walks from a parking lot, so you can stack two or three in a day if you start early.

Late winter and spring after rain give the best flow. Summer weekends fill forest pullouts like Helton Creek early, and Georgia's state park day pass is now $10 per vehicle, so plan parking before you leave the metro.

name: Charlotte
intro: Charlotte sits on the Piedmont, so the waterfalls within a day trip are mostly up in the Blue Ridge and along the South Mountains, not in the city itself. Pearsons Falls near Tryon, about 84 miles west, is a short preserve walk once you book a timed ticket, and Linville Falls on the Blue Ridge Parkway is about 79 miles northwest with multiple overlooks for the Linville River drop.

Farther into the mountains, Crabtree Falls near the Parkway, Cascade Falls and Lower Cascade Falls at Hanging Rock, and Hickorynut Falls above Lake Lure all fit inside a two-hour radius for an early start. Most of these are short hikes or overlook walks, so you can stack two stops if parking cooperates.

Spring after rain is the time to go. Summer weekends fill DuPont-area and Parkway lots early, and privately managed sites like Pearsons Falls require advance tickets, so plan parking and reservations before you leave the metro.

name: Fresno
intro: Fresno is the closest large Central Valley city to Yosemite Valley's big waterfalls. Bridalveil Fall, Vernal Fall and Yosemite Falls all sit about 65 to 70 miles northeast, and Nevada Fall continues up the Mist Trail beyond Vernal. A single park day can cover Bridalveil's short paved walk and a Mist Trail hike if you start early and use the Valley shuttle.

Outside Yosemite, Tokopah Falls in Sequoia National Park and Rainbow Falls near Mammoth Lakes stretch the same day-trip radius in other directions. Closer foothill stops such as Corlieu Falls and Angel Falls near Oakhurst fill shorter half-days when you want to skip park entrance lines.

Snowmelt makes late spring and early summer the strongest season in the Sierra. Yosemite charges a vehicle entrance fee, Mist Trail dogs are not allowed, and Valley parking fills on peak weekends, so check current entrance and shuttle details before you drive.

name: Nashville
intro: Nashville sits on the edge of some of the best waterfall country in the Southeast. Head east toward the Cumberland Plateau and the Highland Rim and the streams start dropping over limestone and sandstone ledges, which is why so many of the falls on this page are within a 60- to 90-minute drive of downtown.

The closest is Jackson Falls, right off the Natchez Trace Parkway at milepost 404.7 southwest of the city, where a short, steep paved path drops to the pool. Stillhouse Hollow Falls near Summertown is another easy half-day. Going east, Burgess Falls and Cummins Falls are the classic pair. Cummins requires a Gorge Access Permit, bought in advance, to go down to the base. Fall Creek Falls State Park, with Cane Creek and Piney Creek Falls, is worth a full day, as is the long hike to Virgin Falls.
Flow peaks from winter through spring. Many plateau streams drop low in late summer and fall, so check recent rainfall before a long drive.

name: Boston
intro: Boston is not a big-waterfall city, and the falls within 100 miles are smaller and quieter than the ones in the White Mountains farther north. Most of them sit in wooded state and land-trust reservations in central and western Massachusetts, southern New Hampshire, Rhode Island and eastern Connecticut. They make good half-day or full-day trips, especially in spring.

The nearest on this list is Danforth Falls in Hudson, about 27 miles west of downtown in a straight line. In the Royalston area of north-central Massachusetts, Doane's Falls and Royalston Falls are both free Trustees properties. Doane's Falls bans swimming and wading, and the trail into Royalston Falls is steep and slippery. Stepstone Falls in western Rhode Island and Chapman Falls in Connecticut's Devil's Hopyard State Park are good to the south. Glendale Falls in the Berkshire foothills is one of the longest runs in the state.
Snowmelt in April and May brings the most water. By August many of these brooks are thin, and some parking areas are not plowed in winter.

name: Washington
intro: The best waterfall near Washington, DC is barely outside the Beltway. The Great Falls of the Potomac, about 14 miles from downtown in a straight line, drops through a rocky gorge that you can see from the Olmsted Island boardwalk on the Maryland side in Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park. It is an easy half-day trip, and the boardwalk is accessible.

For a full day, head west to Shenandoah National Park. Dark Hollow Falls, Rose River Falls and Whiteoak Canyon are all off Skyline Drive in the park's Central District, and Overall Run Falls, the tallest in the park at 93 feet, is reached from Mathews Arm in the North District. These are real hikes with climbs of roughly 400 to 1,300 feet, and the park charges a $30 vehicle entrance fee good for seven days. North of the city, Cunningham Falls State Park near Thurmont, Maryland, has a short Lower Trail and a fully accessible boardwalk to its 78-foot cascade.
Spring and the days after a soaking rain are the best times to go. Several Shenandoah falls, Overall Run in particular, can slow to a trickle in a dry summer or fall.

name: Denver
intro: The waterfalls near Denver are mountain falls fed by snowmelt, and most of them are in or near Rocky Mountain National Park, about an hour or more from the city. The closest on this list, Elk Falls in Staunton State Park, is roughly 28 miles southwest of downtown in a straight line but takes a long day hike of about 12 miles to reach. Boulder Falls in Boulder Canyon is closer to the road, but the City of Boulder has kept it closed since a 2024 rockfall while it designs a new viewing platform.

In Rocky Mountain National Park, Copeland Falls is a flat 0.6-mile round trip from the Wild Basin Trailhead, and the same trail continues to Ouzel Falls at 2.7 miles each way. Alberta Falls is a 1.6-mile round trip from Glacier Gorge on Bear Lake Road, Chasm Falls is a short walk from Old Fall River Road, and Adams Falls is an easy stroll from the East Inlet Trailhead in Grand Lake. Pets are not allowed on park trails, and from late May to mid-October you may need a timed entry reservation as well as an entrance pass. To the south, Helen Hunt Falls in North Cheyenne Cañon Park near Colorado Springs is a roadside stop.
June and early July bring the biggest flow. Many high trails stay icy into late spring, and Old Fall River Road closes for the winter.
